description: Applies the FSharp.Refactor analyzers' quick fixes to F# code from the command line. Point it at a project, a script, a solution, a directory or a glob; --dry-run reports without editing.
releaseNotes: 0.8.3: FR0147 (repeated qualified names become an open), FR0146 (unparametrized SQL), a priority flag on the likely-defect rules, notes only review mode, workspace targets, HTML and CSV reports, editor quick-fix offers for FR0032, FR0038, FR0046, FR0047, FR0055, FR0061, FR0062, FR0079, FR0089 and FR0105, FR0066 widened to helpers and one-hop strings, FR0120 and FR0124 across Microsoft.Extensions.Logging, Serilog and Logary, FR0127 connection strings and tokens, FR0075 and FR0028 false positives removed, alternative fixes as separate messages; 0.8.2: FR0077 (missing interface members) offers a second fix in the editor: stubs returning the empty value of each member type instead of raising. New rule FR0145: a record expression that leaves fields unassigned (FS0764) gets them, each with the empty value its type makes obvious (None, [], Map.empty, ...) - applied by the sweep - or a NotImplementedException placeholder and, in the editor, a zero-value alternative (false, 0, Unchecked.defaultof) where no default is obvious. New rule FR0144: a script #r or #I path the package no longer has (net451 to net461, netstandard1.6 to netstandard2.0, a bumped version folder) is re-pointed at what the package has now, ranked for the runtime the original implies (netcoreapp only as a last resort); the other candidates are listed. New rule FR0143: a script whose #load chain misses a file of the project it loads from gets it loaded in the project order, read off the FS0039 the compiler already reports and the fsproj compile items; a missing namespace from a ProjectReference gets a #r to its built assembly. It runs on scripts that do not typecheck, which is its input. FR0086 reads the callee signature from the typed tree: a hole-free interpolated string passed to printfn (or any function without a FormattableString parameter) loses its dollar; only a callee that takes one, or an unresolved one, keeps it. Scripts that use fsi (fsi.CommandLineArgs) typecheck again: the fsi auxiliary assembly is referenced from the SDK the script directory resolves, since the tool does not ship it; a script that still does not typecheck now prints its first errors. Every rule runs on a worker with a 64 MB stack: a walker whose depth follows the shape of the code (a long statement chain, a long operator chain) can no longer overflow the 1 MB host thread and take FsAutoComplete or the sweep down with it. A project path given relative to the current directory works again (the build runs from the project directory since 0.7.7, and the relative path did not survive the move). New Rules.md: every rule on one line with a from-to example, its default state and whether the fix needs --api-changes; the tests keep it complete. FR0070 leaves a record a class when its fields are read inside a quotation or query block, since a captured struct local cannot have a field read there (Linq.Expression.Optimizer). FR0116 gives a record-building member that leaves its let rec group the parameter and return types the group inferred for it, since a label shared between records no longer determines the type on its own (fedit); without the typed tree such a member stays. FR0092 (failwith context) applies its fix only with --api-changes: exception text is observable behaviour that tests assert on, so a plain sweep now reports it as an advisory note. FR0013 and FR0094 keep the parentheses of a unit argument: m (()) passes unit as a value, m () is a call with no arguments. New rule FR0142: a test (Fact, Theory, Test, TestCase, TestMethod) whose body blocks on async work - Async.RunSynchronously, .Result, .Wait(), GetAwaiter().GetResult() on a Task - returns the work instead, the body becoming a task block cast to System.Threading.Tasks.Task with each blocking statement a bind, so xUnit, NUnit and MSTest await it and the thread is free while the work is in flight; a test method shape is the framework business, so this is not an API change. Builds run from the project own directory, so the repository global.json governs SDK resolution as it would for the developer; where the pinned SDK is not installed the build falls back to a neutral directory and says so, naming the pin. FR0140 stands down on a construction whose argument is not parenthesised, FR0086 keeps the dollar of a hole-free interpolation where a FormattableString is expected, and FR0050 hands the fold its tuple first when the body looks up a member on the accumulator - three rollbacks found sweeping Fable. From FsAutoComplete: FR0006 binds a wildcard where the clause body never reads the guard variable (FS1182 under warnings-as-errors), FR0008 leaves an active pattern tuple input alone, and FR0086 keeps the dollar of a hole-free interpolation passed to any function, since an F# parameter typed FormattableString has nothing in its spelling to say so. From FSharp.Data: FR0085 keeps new on a type application with static arguments (a type provider such as CsvProvider) - the bare form parses as a comparison - and treats a provided type as of unknown disposability, since what it erases to is where IDisposable lives. FR0119 now sees a blocking call inside a match arm, an if branch, a try body or a loop body of the same computation expression: its statement-spine walk stopped at control flow, and CarmelNet ReadToEnd two arms deep was never offered its async twin. From Nu and PethostBackup: FR0101 keeps an indexed loop whose body takes the address of the element, FR0030 keeps a loop whose receiver list is chosen per element, and FR0092 consults the interpolation gate (F# 5 syntax and an FSharp.Core that backs it) before rewriting a failwith message. A hint matched against a pipeline is rendered back as a pipeline - xs |> M.collect f rather than M.collect f xs - so the head is typed before any lambda among the arguments is checked; the application form met "Lookup on object of indeterminate type" wherever the lambda looked up a member on its parameter (Fable, Nu, PethostBackup). From the tree-sitter-fsharp corpora and welendus: FR0009 offers Result.defaultValue, defaultWith, isOk and isError only where FSharp.Core is 9 or newer, FR0031 renders a backtick-quoted identifier verbatim in its hole, and a pass whose check reports errors is checked a second time before blame - a type provider that loses its connection between two checks made every provided type undefined for one check and cost welendus 493 fixes. FR0074 checks the flattened path head against every module, namespace and type in scope, not only the types this file declares: a field named after the module holding its type (Settings: Settings.GameSettings, on Nu) resolved as the module and the record as the wrong type. Two SwaggerProvider failures were the tool, not the project. The first build of a multi-targeted project restored with the analysed framework as a global property, which writes an assets file for that framework alone, and everything that later built another - the all-frameworks verification, a sibling project building this one through an MSBuild task - failed with NETSDK1005 or a half-resolved reference set, putting good fixes back run after run; restore now runs separately and without the framework. And a project that names no FSharp.Core (DisableImplicitFSharpCoreReference, the paket convention) was typechecked against the FSharp.Core loaded in the tool process, a netstandard2.1 build, where fsc quietly uses the netstandard2.0 build bundled in the SDK: three IAsyncDisposable errors the project never had. The compiler own FSharp.Core is now added whenever the arguments carry none. FR0004 reads the callback rather than the whole function: a function that assigns into its array in a loop and then filters it with a lambda that only reads - the ordinary imperative shape - moves again, while a lambda that assigns, a local closure that assigns, or a function handed the collection itself still keeps the eager copy. FR0130 and FR0133 are back on by default: they had described themselves as off while running on every sweep, and the Literal attributes and backtick names a sweep produced were the behaviour users had; a repository that finds either churn turns it off in fsharprefactor.json. FR0130, FR0133 and FR0016 now edit the companion signature in step, through the mechanism FR0022 introduced: the .fsi val gains the Literal attribute and the value it must then spell out, the renamed val takes its backtick spelling, the type gains its Struct attribute - one atomic edit set spanning both files, or, where the signature cannot be read (editors install no cross-file parser), a fix for a non-private declaration is withheld rather than offered half-done; private declarations, which no signature mentions, are unaffected. 0.7.6: --api-changes now rewrites call sites in scripts. A .fsx that #loads a project source compiles that file INTO itself, so it sees the internal bindings this pass is allowed to reshape - while being a separate compilation whose calls never appear in the project symbol tables, so the pass own "every use resolves or the change is abandoned" guard never fired and the script simply stopped compiling. Scripts under the scanned path are now indexed, matched to the project by declaration position rather than by name (a referenced assembly can carry the same full name), and rewritten with the definition. Nothing verifies a script edit otherwise - dotnet build compiles the project, not the .fsx beside it - so every edited script is typechecked afterwards and a broken one takes its whole suggestion back, the uninvolved groups re-applying from the restored text. A script that does not typecheck to begin with is unreadable, so nothing it loads is reshaped at all. FR0140 was costing 77 percent of all analyzer time on a large project (51 seconds of 66): its typed constructor lookup sat in the match guard and charged an FCS symbol resolution for every single-line let binding in the file, before anything asked whether a property assignment even followed. Cheap syntactic gates first, typed lookups last, identical findings. FR0117 keeps each arm own comment when it folds arms into an or-pattern: F# accepts comments between the alternatives and fantomas leaves them there, so an arm carrying a comment no longer has to be held back - it was the most often correctly silent rule in the catalogue, and on one corpus this turns zero applied fixes into eight. FR0013 no longer strips the parentheses inside a shorthand lambda: _.reshape(a) is atomic and _.reshape a is not, so six fixes went in on a real repository, broke the build and were rolled back. Output now carries colour where the terminal has one: progress and timings recede, work that landed is green, a deliberate stand-down is distinct from a failure, advice with no fix behind it has its own colour, and every line still says in words what it is. Redirected streams, NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb and --no-color all stay plain. Argument diagnostics say what is actually wrong: a value-taking flag given without its value no longer reads as an unknown flag, a second bare path is named as a second target, and --codes validates against the catalogue instead of silently matching nothing when a code is mistyped. FR0060 stops merging past four attributes or the wrap column, both configurable per repository as maxAttributes and wrapColumn. A fix held back because a comment sits inside its span no longer prints: code carrying a comment is already good F#, nothing is wrong and nothing is deferred. An ignored-path skip names the files when there are fewer than nine of them, base names only, so a short list says which file was passed over rather than only how many. Sweeping toro, nu, fcs-fable, SQLProvider, FSharp.Finance.Personal and Fuuga surfaced one hazard under five rules: a name that means one thing applied and another thing referenced. FR0003 no longer composes an operator or a method with optional parameters as a bare stage - (-) is not the subtraction that was written, and a bare method loses its defaults. FR0012 leaves an equality sitting directly in an argument list alone: a named argument such as AutoReset = true parses as one, and only the typechecker knows better. FR0085 keeps new wherever the bare name would resolve to something else - a union case of the same name, a sibling type of the same name in the declaring module, or a type of another arity in any fragment of the namespace across every referenced assembly, which is how Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstractions declares ChatResponse while Microsoft.Extensions.AI declares the generic one and the bare name picks by reference order. FR0095 declines id, fst and snd where the file binds that name itself. FR0140 stands down on a type-annotated constructor argument, after which a comma ends the type instead of introducing a property. FR0004 keeps a conversion in place where the code between it and its target mutates anything, since a Seq.toList in front of a loop that edits the collection is the guard against the enumeration being modified. Signature files now count: FR0022 renames a union-case field in the .fsi beside the .fs, and FR0069, FR0093 and FR0130 stand down where a signature would disagree. FR0130 and FR0133, documented as off by default, now are. The signature gate now lives in the scope check FR0011, FR0016, FR0069, FR0093 and FR0134 share: beside a .fsi, which declares every internal declaration too, only a private declaration may change shape. FR0085 counts the fragments a name is split across rather than its declarations, so TaskCompletionSource, Lazy and any type beside its own generic twin in one assembly keep their fix - only the cross-assembly split is the hazard. FR0004 asks who owns the collection before moving an operation that takes a callback: one the function binds itself - a local, a parameter, a loop or match variable - can only be written from the function own text, which is read in full for an assignment, while a module-level or captured collection can be written by any function the callback names and is left alone. Operations taking no callback, and list or array literals, move as before. FR0095 reads scope rather than the whole file: a let id = 42 in one function no longer costs every other function its fix, while a rebinding on the path or a module-level one declared above still does. 0.7.5: a capability fix now stands down where it has nowhere safe to live. On a pass over a framework wider than the project narrowest target, such a fix belongs inside the project own framework guard or nowhere: where the project offers no framework-shaped constant, FR0038, FR0039 and FR0106 keep their advice and drop the edit rather than going in plainly and being reverted by the all-frameworks build - which took every innocent fix in those files with it, 62 applied and 7 files put back on SwaggerProvider. FR0119 asks the same question in full: its gate read only the case where a guard exists that its multi-edit swap cannot pair with, and missed the case of no guard at all, so it took Dispose to DisposeAsync on a project whose netstandard2.0 target has no such interface. Re-sweeping that repository now applies 59 fixes, keeps every one, and leaves every target framework building. 0.7.4: fixes from sweeping SQLProvider, which the tool left with a broken build. FR0140 parenthesises the value it moves into a construction: a cast binds looser than the named property, so cmd.Connection then con cast to SqlConnection folded to an equality against an undefined Connection. The all-frameworks arbiter now counts errors both ways rather than asking pass or fail - a project can be broken for two reasons at once, and a pre-existing breakage outside the snapshot made every fix look innocent and put them all back. The generated-file sniff reads thirty lines and knows the prose and attribute forms, not just the XML marker, so a FAKE-written AssemblyInfo is left alone. The Visual Studio extension checks the file rather than trusting the buffer content type: F# sources only, and never a vendored, package or generated path. --parse-only no longer reads framework-conditional DefineConstants, which activated one framework branch and hid the rest. FR0039 pairs with the project own framework guard like FR0038 does, so a StringComparison overload no longer breaks netstandard2.0; FR0119 keeps its advice but withholds the edit where a guard would be needed, its rewrite spanning more than one edit. 0.7.3: FR0141 stays silent inside async and task, where the advice does not hold: a task compiles to a resumable state machine and recursive return! grows the stack, and in async the recursive function must return an Async so the change reaches the signature rather than the loop. FR0141 notes a while loop that carries state forward by mutation and leaves through a boolean flag - tail recursion written inside out. Deliberately not the search loop: a carried value whose every assignment is a counter bump is an index, and that shape already short-circuits and allocates nothing (measured 12x faster than Array.exists on an early hit). Note only. FR0107 documented accurately: it already folds a pure let-prefix into the lambda, which the rule text denied. 140 rules. FR0140 folds property assignments that immediately follow a construction into F#'s named-property construction - not a constructor overload and not faster, the same calls in the same order, but the object reads as constructed rather than assembled and the half-built value stops being nameable. Only the uninterrupted run straight after the binding folds in. 139 rules. SARIF reports now say what kind of finding each one is: every analyzer speaks at the SDK Hint severity, which is its editor channel rather than a judgement, so the report stamped note on all of them and a swallowed exception rendered exactly like a redundant paren in code scanning. The category is what the rules actually decide, so it is what the report carries - correctness earns warning level, the rest stay notes, nothing becomes an error - and each result gains a category property beside fixable, with a tool.driver.rules block so code scanning can group and filter. FR0089 no longer reads the F# 6 indexer spelling as a single-tuple list. Since F# 6, grid[0, 1, 2] parses as an ATOMIC application of a bracket to the thing before it, the same shape as the [ 1, 2 ] paste trap the rule hunts, so every multi-dimensional index raised a false correctness note. The atomic flag is what separates them, and a spaced list argument stays flagged. Found by surveying an agent-generated corpus, where all six of the rule notes in one test file were this and none a real trap. Both index spellings are now locked into the tests across the rule set: every rule that DETECTS indexing already matched the atomic form beside the legacy DotIndexedGet node, and the rest only traverse into brackets. SARIF reports now name the URL the package and --help publish. 0.7.2: FR0139 swaps Seq functions to the Array module where the typed tree proves an array — measured on .NET 10, arrays only, with `contains` on int arrays defaulting to vectorised Enumerable.Contains and offering Array.contains beside it. Rule fixes found by dogfooding and by re-sweeping the corpus: FR0030 no longer emits code that cannot parse for a range source, FR0119 binds only on a computation expression's own statement spine (21 rollbacks in one repo), FR0029 tail extraction stops at a `use` and FR0005 cures the shape an older version wrote, FR0039 keeps backticked receivers, and a failed verification no longer leaves kept fixes suppressed. The benchmarks now target .NET 10. 0.7.1: the published package now reliably carries BOTH analyzer SDK builds flat in analyzers/dotnet/fs — FSharp.Refactor.Analyzers.Ionide.dll for stock Ionide (SDK 0.35.0) and the 0.37.2 build for the CLI and newer FsAutoComplete — plus the review-hardening fixes 0.7.0's rolling pack accumulated; the repository gains a classic Visual Studio extension (VSIX): squiggles and light-bulb fixes in VS 2022-2026 rendered from an FsAutoComplete sidecar. 0.7.0: cross-file migrations arrive — under --api-changes, strictly internal declarations now migrate project-wide with every use classified against its own file (FR0069 voption, FR0093 struct tuples, FR0049 taskify), gated hard: public never, InternalsVisibleTo assemblies never, one unconvertible use vetoes everything. FR0029 grows branch-return tail extraction and per-arm match/match! splitting into nested tasks, and match! arm interiors are finally visible to every rule (an SDK walker hole). Solution runs order narrowest target first and shared directive-free files sweep once across all frameworks and projects; fully-swept compilations skip their typecheck. New rules: FR0132 trailing comments promote to XML docs; FR0133 five-word test names become double-backtick sentences (locals opt-in); FR0134 UtcNow-fed DateTime fields migrate to DateTimeOffset (opt-in); FR0135 markdown-bearing script comments become literate (** cells. FR0022 also mines field names from XAndY case names and clear trailing comments. Everything adversarially audited: keyword field names, fake-clock shadowing, cross-type comparisons, multi-line plain strings under re-indentation, TestCaseSource string references and more are all vetoed by construction. FR0136 states zero-argument Guid constructors as Guid.Empty (the editor also offers NewGuid()); FR0137 fuses consecutive same-module map passes via composition; FR0035 gains the module-level-set quick-fix (in-place Set.ofList when probes are the only uses, a HashSet companion otherwise); FR0039 extends its fix to the method-call shape (path.ToLower().StartsWith "file:" becomes the StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase overload, per the .NET string best-practices guide); FR0005 collapses no-op return! task wrappers and unjustified tail thunks; the multi-pass loop warns on non-convergence and blocks a rule that keeps growing the same file, and a failed verification now rolls back only the fixes at the error sites instead of every fix in the file. FR0138 rewrites hand-rolled emptiness tests (isNull x || x = "") to String.IsNullOrEmpty/IsNullOrWhiteSpace; FR0139 swaps Seq functions to the Array module where the typed tree proves an array (measured 2.3x on exists, enumerator allocation gone) - arrays only, and never the numeric aggregates that FR0041 sends to vectorised LINQ. 138 rules. 0.6.8: fixes first — a run now prints its fixes and holds advisory notes to one summary line (--notes lists them, --report exports SARIF). FR0029 applies its own FS3511 advice: hoisting pre-await lets (documenting comments travel along), splitting branching tasks per arm, wrapping non-awaiting tails, extracting awaiting try/finally suffixes; the multi-pass loop chains the moves. FR0049 rewrites blocking binds (GetAwaiter().GetResult(), .Result, Async.RunSynchronously) to let!/do! in task and async alike; sync-direction swaps stay config-opt-in. Suppression policy (suppressions: all/no-correctness/none plus --honor-suppressions) and per-rule config parameters. New rules FR0117-FR0131: or-pattern arm folding; CancellationToken omission and None-propagation; awaitable-twin calls; catch blocks logging without the exception (PII-aware); DateTime.Now/UtcNow.Date pitfalls; invalid regexes; Monitor.Enter/Exit to lock; interpolated logging to message templates; invisible/bidi Unicode with escape fixes; process-execution sinks; provider-format API-key literals; obsolete crypto constructors to static factories; guard-equality clauses to literal patterns; module constants gain [<Literal>]; provably tail-recursive functions gain [<TailCall>]. match/match!/function parity for arm rules; SHA1 editor alternatives on FR0065. 130 rules.
